title: SaaS Access Management: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: GitHub
steps.what: GitHub: repository collaborator, team membership and team-to-repository, using a personal access token, with GitHub Enterprise Server supported.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: GitLab
steps.what: GitLab: group and project membership with access level, using an administrator token, with self-managed supported.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Salesforce
steps.what: Salesforce: permission sets, permission set groups and profiles, using OAuth JWT bearer with a connected app.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Snowflake
steps.what: Snowflake: role membership, using key-pair authentication.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Databricks
steps.what: Databricks: Unity Catalog privileges, using an OAuth service principal.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Google Workspace
steps.what: Google Workspace: admin role assignment, using a service account with domain-wide delegation.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Approval chains
steps.what: Requests go through multi-level approval chains with automatic routing to the right approver, self-approval blocked and optional auto-approval by policy.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Slack and Mattermost approval
steps.what: Approvers act directly from Slack or Mattermost, while Microsoft Teams, Jira and ServiceNow receive notifications and tickets.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Expiry reaper
steps.what: Every grant carries an expiry, and a reaper reconciles continuously and removes access from the platform when the window closes, even if the original grant workflow is long finished.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Grant receipts
steps.what: Access to the systems engineers actually use is requestable, approved, time-bound and automatically removed, with a receipt for every grant.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.

steps.title: Nightly drift detection
steps.what: Every grant is recorded, reference-counted where several policies overlap, and reconciled against the platform nightly to surface access granted outside Privilege.
steps.why: Standing access accumulates, such as a repository grant for one incident or a warehouse role for one migration.
